books.title: It Is Spring
books.art_why: Spring flowers, worms, plants, birds and animals all exist in the real world and can be photographed today.

pages.text: The Sun pops up. The flowers pop out.
pages.brief: A bright spring sun rising above a green garden, warm light spilling over the grass. In front of it, fresh flowers pushing up out of the soil with petals opening wide. A few small blossoms stand tall in the soft dirt, catching the morning sun, with open sky behind them.

pages.text: The worms pop up. The plants pop up.
pages.brief: Close view of dark garden soil where pink earthworms are wriggling up to the surface. Beside them, small green plants push up through the dirt, their stems and first leaves rising out of the ground. Loose crumbs of soil and a few damp clods sit around the worms and seedlings.

pages.text: The leaves pop out. The birds pop out.
pages.brief: Branches of a tree with fresh green leaves unfurling and opening out along the twigs. Among the new leaves, small birds pop out from the branch, heads and wings showing as they appear from the foliage. Soft spring sky and more budding branches fill the background behind them.

pages.text: The animals pop out. Spring pops out everywhere. Pop, pop, pop.
pages.brief: A wide spring meadow where animals appear all around: a rabbit, a squirrel and other small creatures coming out among the grass and flowers. New leaves and blossoms fill the scene, with birds above and plants below, everything bursting out at once in the open spring sunshine. Pop, pop, pop.

books.title: Trucks
books.art_why: Trucks are real vehicles that exist today and can be photographed.

pages.text: Some trucks carry mail. Some trucks carry animals.
pages.brief: A mail truck with letters and parcels in its back drives on a road, and beside it a truck carries animals in a slatted truck bed. The animals are visible inside. Both trucks are shown outdoors, side by side, doing their carrying jobs.

pages.text: Some trucks carry garbage. Some trucks carry logs.
pages.brief: A garbage truck carries bins or bags of garbage, and another truck carries cut logs stacked in its bed. The two trucks are shown outdoors on a road, side by side, with the garbage load and the log load clearly visible as they do their carrying jobs.

pages.text: Some trucks carry cement. Some trucks carry ice cream.
pages.brief: A cement truck with a rotating drum carries wet cement, and another truck carries ice cream in boxes or tubs. The trucks are outdoors on a road, side by side, showing the cement load and the ice cream load as they do their carrying jobs.

pages.text: Some trucks carry cars. Some trucks carry trucks.
pages.brief: A car-carrier truck carries several cars loaded on its long trailer, and another truck carries a smaller truck on its bed. The trucks are outdoors on a road, side by side, showing the car load and the truck load as they do their carrying jobs.

books.title: Old and New
books.art_why: Pickup trucks, houses, bikes and teddy bears are real objects that can be photographed today.

pages.text: These pickup trucks are old. These pickup trucks are new.
pages.brief: An old pickup truck with dull, weathered paint stands beside a new pickup truck with bright, shiny paint. Both trucks are shown side by side so young readers can compare the old truck and the new truck.

pages.text: These houses are old. These houses are new.
pages.brief: An old house with worn, faded walls stands beside a new house with fresh, clean walls. The two houses are shown side by side, letting young readers compare the older home with the newer home.

pages.text: These bikes are old. These bikes are new.
pages.brief: An old bike with rusty, worn parts stands beside a new bike with clean, shiny parts. The two bikes are shown side by side so young readers can compare the old bicycle and the new bicycle.

pages.text: These teddy bears are old. These teddy bears are new.
pages.brief: An old teddy bear with worn, faded fur sits beside a new teddy bear with soft, fresh fur. The two teddy bears are shown side by side so young readers can compare the old bear and the new bear.

books.title: What Has These Feet?
books.art_why: The book shows real animals—duck, elephant, tiger, and shark—that exist today, so photographs fit best.

pages.text: What kind of animal has these feet? A duck has these little feet.
pages.brief: A duck stands on a plain light background, shown from the side so its small feet are clearly visible. The duck’s body and bill are visible above the feet, and the little feet rest flat on the ground.

pages.text: What kind of animal has these feet? An elephant has these big feet.
pages.brief: An elephant stands on a plain light background, with its large feet shown close to the ground. Its trunk and big body are visible above, and the broad feet look strong and big. The image focuses on the size of the elephant’s feet.

pages.text: What kind of animal has these feet? A tiger has these soft feet.
pages.brief: A tiger stands on a plain light background, shown from the side so its soft-looking feet are visible. Its body and head are partly visible above the feet, and the paws rest quietly on the ground. The focus is on the tiger’s soft feet.

pages.text: What kind of animal has no feet? A shark has no feet.
pages.brief: A shark swims in clear blue water, shown from the side with its whole body visible. It has fins and a tail but no feet at all. The shark’s body is smooth and long, and the water around it is plain and open.

books.title: Are These His or Hers?
books.art_why: Real everyday clothes that exist today photograph clearly.

pages.text: Are these clothes his or hers? These socks are his.
pages.brief: A tidy pile of everyday clothes rests on a bed in a bright bedroom, with a pair of plain socks laid neatly on top, side by side and easy to see. More clothes sit folded beside them, ready to be sorted into two groups.

pages.text: These shorts are hers. These pajamas are his.
pages.brief: On a bedroom floor in daylight, a pair of shorts lies spread out flat beside a pair of pajamas. The two garments sit apart from each other in clear view, set out as if someone has just sorted them into two separate piles.

pages.text: These shirts are hers. These jackets are his.
pages.brief: Two shirts hang or lie flat on one side of a table in a sunlit room, while two jackets rest on the other side. The clothes are spread apart and clearly visible, arranged in two groups for someone to look at and compare.

pages.text: These hats are hers. Are these jeans his or hers? They are his and hers.
pages.brief: Two hats sit together on a low shelf in a bright hallway, and a pair of jeans lies folded open on the floor below them. The clothes are set out plainly, one group above and one below, ready to be looked at.

books.title: Rain in the Country
books.art_why: Real outdoor weather, a horse, mud and puddles are all things a camera can capture today.

pages.text: I see the clouds.
pages.brief: A wide view of open countryside under a grey, heavy sky, with thick dark clouds rolling in above green fields and a few trees. No rain has started yet, and the land looks still and quiet, waiting for the storm to arrive.

pages.text: I see the rain.
pages.brief: Rain falls steadily over the same country fields, streaking down in visible lines. Grass bends under the drops and small splashes rise from the ground, while the grey sky stays low overhead and the trees stand dark and wet in the distance.

pages.text: I see the lightning.
pages.brief: A bright fork of lightning splits the dark storm sky above the country fields, lighting up the clouds for a moment. The fields and trees below are dim and shadowed, and rain still comes down in the distance.

pages.text: I see the horse.
pages.brief: A horse stands out in the open country field during the rain, coat wet and dark, head turned as it stands calmly on the grass. Fence posts and a few trees show behind it under the grey cloudy sky.

pages.text: I see the puddle.
pages.brief: A shallow puddle lies in the wet grass of the country field, holding grey sky and a bit of light on its surface. Wet grass leans around the edges, and a few raindrops still ripple the water.

pages.text: I see the mud.
pages.brief: Soft brown mud fills the ground in the country field, churned and glossy with rainwater, with deep marks and small pools in it. Wet grass grows along the edge, and the damp earth stretches back toward the trees.

pages.text: I see the rainbow.
pages.brief: A wide rainbow arches across the clearing country sky above the green fields and trees. The rain has eased, the clouds are breaking into lighter grey and white, and the wet grass below shines.

pages.text: I see the Sun.
pages.brief: The Sun comes out bright over the country field, shining through the last thin clouds. Wet grass and the puddle sparkle in the light, the trees stand clear and green, and the sky above is opening up.

books.title: Boats
books.art_why: Real boats exist today and can be photographed.

pages.text: This boat carries people.
pages.brief: A wide, clear view of a passenger boat on calm water, with several people standing and sitting on its deck as the boat carries them across. The boat is the main subject, shown in daylight, with open water around it.

pages.text: This boat carries police.
pages.brief: A police boat moves across calm water in daylight. Police officers are aboard the boat as it carries them, and the boat is shown clearly from the side so young readers can see it is a working police vessel on the water.

pages.text: This boat carries food.
pages.brief: A small cargo boat on calm water, loaded with food on its deck. The food is visible as the boat carries it across the water in daylight, with the boat shown clearly and simply from the side.

pages.text: This boat carries logs.
pages.brief: A working boat on calm water carries a load of long logs stacked on its deck. The logs are the main cargo, and the boat is shown in daylight from a clear side view as it moves across the water.

pages.text: This boat carries trash.
pages.brief: A utility boat on calm water carries trash heaped on its deck. The boat is shown clearly in daylight, with the load of trash visible as it moves across the water, making the boat's job easy for young readers to see.

pages.text: This boat carries cars.
pages.brief: A large car ferry on calm water carries several cars on its open deck. The cars are parked and visible as the ferry moves across the water in daylight, with the whole boat shown clearly from the side.

pages.text: This boat carries planes.
pages.brief: A wide transport boat on calm water carries an airplane on its deck. The plane is visible as the boat moves across the water in daylight, with the large vessel shown clearly from a side view.

pages.text: This boat carries boats.
pages.brief: A large carrier boat on calm water carries smaller boats on its deck. The smaller boats are visible as cargo while the large boat moves across the water in daylight, shown clearly from the side so the carrying boat and its load can be seen.

books.title: Beach Fun
books.art_why: A real beach with real children swimming, digging and flying kites exists today, so photographs are possible.

pages.text: We swim at the beach. We dig at the beach.
pages.brief: Two young children in swimsuits splash and swim in shallow blue water at a sunny beach, arms out as they paddle. Nearby on the dry sand, the same children kneel with small plastic spades, digging a hole and piling sand beside it. Gentle waves and a wide empty shoreline behind them.

pages.text: We run at the beach. We eat at the beach.
pages.brief: Children run barefoot along the wet sand at the edge of the waves, feet kicking up spray, a beach bag and towel left behind on the sand. In the next moment they sit on a spread towel eating sandwiches and fruit from a lunch box, seagulls in the distance.

pages.text: We play at the beach. We fly kites at the beach.
pages.brief: Children play together on the sand, tossing a ball and laughing near a pile of buckets. Above them two colourful kites lift into a bright blue sky on long strings, the children tilting their heads back and holding the strings as the kites climb higher over the beach.

pages.text: We find shells at the beach. We build castles at the beach.
pages.brief: A child crouches on the sand holding a spiral shell up to look at it, a small collection of shells in a bucket nearby. Beside them, children pat wet sand into a castle with towers and a bucket-shaped top, a spade stuck in the sand next to the wall.

books.title: High or Low?
books.art_why: Real balloons, slides, birds, boards, kites, hoops, cats and people can all be photographed.

pages.text: Are these balloons high or low? Are these slides high or low?
pages.brief: A cluster of balloons floats at different heights above a playground, while two slides stand nearby, one tall and one low. The scene sets up a simple comparison between things that are high and things that are low.

pages.text: Are these birds high or low? Are these boards high or low?
pages.brief: Several birds fly high in the sky, while long boards rest lower down on the ground. The birds and boards are placed together in one view so readers can decide which ones are high and which are low.

pages.text: Are these kites high or low? Are these hoops high or low?
pages.brief: Kites sail high in the open air, and hoops sit lower in the same outdoor scene. The kites and hoops appear together, giving a clear chance to compare what is high and what is low.

pages.text: Are these cats high or low? Are these people high or low?
pages.brief: Cats and people appear in one outdoor scene at different heights, with some positioned higher and some lower. The picture invites readers to look at each cat and each person and decide whether they are high or low.

books.title: Halloween Costumes
books.art_why: Real children in real Halloween costumes exist and can be photographed today.

pages.text: I look like a flower.
pages.brief: A young child stands in a bright room wearing a flower costume, with big fabric petals around the head and a green stem-like body. She holds her arms out to the sides and smiles at the viewer, standing on a plain floor.

pages.text: I look like a bat.
pages.brief: A child stands indoors in a bat costume, with dark wings spread wide from the arms and small pointed ears on the headband. The child grins at the camera with arms lifted, showing the wings stretched out in a hallway.

pages.text: I look like a clown.
pages.brief: A child dressed as a clown stands in a living room, with a colourful wig, a round red nose and a baggy suit. The clown holds both hands up happily, big shoes on the carpet, facing the viewer with a wide smile.

pages.text: I look like a superhero.
pages.brief: A child stands in a costume superhero outfit with a cape flowing behind and a mask over the eyes, hands on hips. The cape lifts slightly as the child poses in a room, chest proud, looking straight at the viewer.

pages.text: I look like a tiger.
pages.brief: A child in a tiger costume crouches on the floor, with an orange striped suit, a hood with small round ears and a long tail. The child's hands are curled like paws on the carpet, face turned to the viewer.

pages.text: I look like a pirate.
pages.brief: A child dressed as a pirate stands in a room wearing a tricorn hat, a striped shirt and a wide belt, with a toy sword at the side. One hand is raised in a cheerful wave toward the viewer.

pages.text: I look like a dragon.
pages.brief: A child in a dragon costume stands with green scaled fabric, small wings on the back and a spiky hood, arms out to the sides. The child faces the viewer in a bright room, mouth open in a playful roar.

pages.text: What is this costume?
pages.brief: A child stands facing the viewer in a costume, arms slightly out, filling the frame in a bright room. The costume is shown clearly from head to toe so the reader can look closely at all its parts.

books.title: Things Made of Wood
books.art_why: Trees and wooden objects such as chairs, puzzles, houses, bridges, boats, fences and toys are real things that can be photographed.

pages.text: Wood comes from trees. Chairs can be made of wood.
pages.brief: A tall tree with a thick trunk and green leaves stands in a calm outdoor setting, showing where wood comes from. Nearby, a simple wooden chair sits on the ground, with a clear wooden seat and back.

pages.text: Puzzles can be made of wood. Houses can be made of wood.
pages.brief: Wooden puzzle pieces lie partly fitted together on a flat surface, showing a puzzle made of wood. A few pieces are joined, and others wait nearby. In the background, a wooden house stands outdoors, with wooden walls and a wooden roof.

pages.text: Bridges can be made of wood. Boats can be made of wood.
pages.brief: A wooden bridge crosses a calm small stream outdoors, with a simple railing and planks clearly made of wood. Nearby on the water, a wooden boat floats, showing another thing that can be made of wood.

pages.text: Fences can be made of wood. Toys can be made of wood.
pages.brief: A wooden fence runs along the edge of a yard outdoors, with upright posts and rails made of wood. On the ground nearby, several wooden toys sit together, showing toys that can be made of wood.

books.title: How Many Legs?
books.art_why: Real animals with visible legs are best shown in photographs.

pages.text: Many animals have legs. These animals have two legs.
pages.brief: A bright outdoor scene shows a mixed group of animals that each stand on two legs, gathered on open ground with grass and sky behind them. Some face left and some face right, legs clearly visible, bodies simple and natural, with space around each animal so their two legs are easy to see.

pages.text: These animals have four legs. 6 These animals have six legs.
pages.brief: An outdoor scene shows two separate groups of animals. The first group stands on four legs, bodies low and steady. Nearby, the second group stands on six legs, smaller legs arranged in pairs beneath their bodies. Grass and open sky keep both groups clear, with every leg visible.

pages.text: These animals have eight legs. These animals have ten legs.
pages.brief: An outdoor scene shows two more groups of animals. One group stands on eight legs, with legs spread out around each body. Beside them, the other group stands on ten legs, with many thin legs visible beneath and around their bodies. Grass and open sky keep every leg easy to see.

pages.text: These animals have many legs. How many legs do these animals have?
pages.brief: An outdoor scene shows a group of animals with many legs, legs overlapping and spreading in all directions around their bodies. The animals fill the open ground, with grass and sky behind them. Their many legs are clearly visible, and space around the group keeps the scene open and clear.

books.title: Healthy Snacks
books.art_why: The book shows real foods that exist today.

pages.text: Apples can be healthy.
pages.brief: A bright close-up photo of fresh red apples, whole and halved, filling the frame. Their skin looks crisp and shiny, and the pale fruit inside looks juicy. The apples are shown alone as the clear, simple subject.

pages.text: Celery can be healthy.
pages.brief: A bright close-up photo of fresh green celery stalks, crisp and clean, filling the frame. The long ribs and small leaves are clearly visible, looking crunchy. The celery is shown alone as the clear, simple subject.

pages.text: Nuts can be healthy.
pages.brief: A bright close-up photo of a pile of mixed nuts, filling the frame. Some nuts look smooth, some look rough, and their shapes and colors are clearly visible. The nuts are shown alone as the clear, simple subject.

pages.text: Seeds can be healthy.
pages.brief: A bright close-up photo of a small pile of edible seeds, filling the frame. The tiny seeds show different shapes and shades, looking clean and ready to eat. The seeds are shown alone as the clear, simple subject.

pages.text: Cheese can be healthy.
pages.brief: A bright close-up photo of cheese, with a block and a few slices filling the frame. The cheese looks firm and creamy, with a clear, simple shape. The cheese is shown alone as the clear, simple subject.

pages.text: Carrots can be healthy.
pages.brief: A bright close-up photo of fresh orange carrots, whole and cut, filling the frame. The carrots look crisp and bright, with their natural shape clearly visible. The carrots are shown alone as the clear, simple subject.

pages.text: Cereal can be healthy.
pages.brief: A bright close-up photo of cereal pieces, filling the frame. The small pieces show different shapes and colors, looking dry and ready to eat. The cereal is shown alone as the clear, simple subject.

pages.text: Healthy snacks taste good!
pages.brief: A bright close-up photo of a variety of healthy snacks, looking fresh and tasty, filling the frame with many colors and shapes. The snacks are shown together as a clear, simple subject, inviting and good to eat.

books.title: What Gives Cover?
books.art_why: All subjects exist in the real world today.

pages.text: A tent gives cover. A tree gives cover.
pages.brief: An outdoor scene with a small camping tent standing on open grass and a tall leafy tree nearby. The tent's fabric slopes down to the ground, making a sheltered space, while the tree's wide branches spread out above the grass, giving cover below them. No people are present.

pages.text: A cave gives cover. A log gives cover.
pages.brief: A rocky hillside with a dark cave opening in the stone. Beside the cave, a thick fallen log lies on the ground among low plants. The cave mouth forms a hollow shelter in the rock, and the log rests on the earth, offering cover along its length. No people are present.

pages.text: An umbrella gives cover. A mushroom gives cover.
pages.brief: An open umbrella stands upright on the ground outdoors, its canopy spread wide. Nearby, a rounded mushroom grows from the grass, its broad cap held above a short stem. The umbrella makes a dry space beneath it, and the mushroom's cap spreads over the ground below. No people are present.

pages.text: A house gives cover. Even a leaf gives cover.
pages.brief: A house stands outdoors with a roof and walls, beside a single broad green leaf growing low to the ground. The house forms a solid shelter, while the wide leaf stretches out above the soil, making a small covered space beneath it. No people are present.

books.title: Where Is Water?
books.art_why: Rivers, lakes, oceans, clouds, pools and underground water are real things a camera can show.

pages.text: Water is all around us. Water is in rivers.
pages.brief: A wide outdoor view of a river flowing between green grassy banks, with water filling the river and spreading across the surrounding land. The river winds into the distance under a soft sky, showing water all around in the natural landscape.

pages.text: Water is in lakes. Water is in the ocean.
pages.brief: A calm lake sits among low hills, its surface still and blue. Beyond the lake, the wide ocean stretches to the horizon with gentle waves. The scene shows two large bodies of water, one close and one far, under an open sky.

pages.text: Water is in the sky. Water is in the pool.
pages.brief: Clouds gather in the sky with rain falling from them, and below, a blue swimming pool holds still water. The sky above and the pool below both show water in different places, outdoors on a clear day.

pages.text: Water is under the ground. Where do you see water?
pages.brief: A cutaway view of the ground shows soil and rock layers, with water pooled in spaces deep beneath the surface. The underground water sits below the grassy top, visible in the dark earth layers.

books.title: The Aquarium
books.art_why: Real aquarium animals and tanks can be photographed.

pages.text: Fish swim in this tank. Rays glide in this tank.
pages.brief: Inside a large aquarium tank, several fish swim through the water, their bodies moving in different directions. Nearby, flat rays glide smoothly past them through the same tank. The scene shows the fish swimming and the rays gliding, all clearly visible in the water.

pages.text: Otters turn in this tank. Jellyfish float in this tank.
pages.brief: In an aquarium tank, otters turn in the water, twisting their bodies as they move around. Nearby, jellyfish float gently through the tank, their soft shapes drifting in the water. The scene shows the otters turning and the jellyfish floating, sharing the tank space.

pages.text: Turtles eat in this tank. Seals flip in this tank.
pages.brief: In a tank at the aquarium, turtles eat, their heads lowered toward food in the water. Nearby, seals flip through the water, bodies curving as they turn over. The scene shows the turtles eating and the seals flipping, both kinds of animals visible in the same tank.

pages.text: Dolphins play in this tank. Whales dive in this tank.
pages.brief: In a large aquarium tank, dolphins play, moving together through the water. Nearby, whales dive down through the tank, their large bodies heading deeper. The scene shows the dolphins playing and the whales diving, all visible in the tank as they move through the water.

books.title: Near and Far Away
books.art_why: Real animals can be photographed.

pages.text: This lion is near.
pages.brief: A lion is shown close to the viewer, large and clear in the foreground. It fills much of the picture, with open space around it, so the animal looks near and easy to see. The lion is the only animal on the page.

pages.text: That lion is far away.
pages.brief: A lion is shown far away, small in the distance. A wide stretch of the scene lies between the viewer and the animal, so the lion looks far off and much less close than before.

pages.text: This owl is near. That owl is far away.
pages.brief: An owl is shown near the viewer, large and clear in the foreground. Farther back, another owl is shown far away, small in the distance. The two owls make the near-and-far contrast easy to see.

pages.text: This wolf is near.
pages.brief: A wolf is shown close to the viewer, large and clear in the foreground. It fills much of the picture, with space around it, so the animal looks near and easy to see. The wolf is the only animal on the page.

pages.text: That wolf is far away.
pages.brief: A wolf is shown far away, small in the distance. A wide stretch of the scene lies between the viewer and the animal, so the wolf looks far off and much less close than before.

pages.text: This deer is near.
pages.brief: A deer is shown close to the viewer, large and clear in the foreground. It fills much of the picture, with open space around it, so the animal looks near and easy to see. The deer is the only animal on the page.

pages.text: That deer is far away.
pages.brief: A deer is shown far away, small in the distance. A wide stretch of the scene lies between the viewer and the animal, so the deer looks far off and much less close than before.

books.title: Amazing Caves
books.art_why: Real caves, bats, crystals, worms, fish and old cave drawings exist today and can be photographed.

pages.text: This cave has sharp rocks. This cave has blue water.
pages.brief: Inside a rocky cave, jagged sharp rocks jut from the walls and floor, catching dim light. Nearby, a still pool of bright blue water fills a hollow in the cave floor. The scene shows only the rough cave rock and the blue water, with no people or animals present.

pages.text: This cave has black bats. This cave has big crystals.
pages.brief: In a dark cave, several black bats hang clustered on the rocky ceiling above. Below them, large crystals rise from the cave floor, big and clear, reflecting faint light. The bats stay close together while the crystals stand in the cave's shadowy space.

pages.text: This cave has bright worms. This cave has old drawings.
pages.brief: In a cave, bright worms glow on the rocky walls or floor, small and luminous. On the cave wall nearby, old drawings show simple marks made long ago. The glowing worms and the old drawings share the same rocky cave setting, with no people present.

pages.text: This cave has shiny fish. What does this cave have?
pages.brief: In a cave pool, shiny fish swim through clear water, their scales catching light. Around them, dark cave rock frames the water. The fish are the focus in this cave, with rocky walls and a shadowed cave space nearby.

books.title: Pond Life
books.art_why: Ponds, fish, snails, ducks, turtles, beavers and children all exist in the real world today, so real photographs match the book.

pages.text: There are plants in the pond. There are fish in the pond.
pages.brief: A still green pond full of water. Tall reeds and leafy water plants stand at the edge and under the surface. Several small fish swim between the stems in the shallow water, their bodies turned sideways as they glide past the plants.

pages.text: There are snails in the pond. There are bugs in the pond.
pages.brief: A close look at the pond water. Small snails creep along a wet stone and a broad green leaf, their shells curled on their backs. Water bugs skate across the surface nearby, thin legs dimpling the water, with more plants and mud below them.

pages.text: There are ducks in the pond. There are turtles in the pond.
pages.brief: A sunny pond bank. Two ducks paddle near the edge, one dipping its bill toward the water. A turtle rests on a flat rock at the shore, its shell in the sunlight, with reeds and plants growing behind it.

pages.text: There are beavers in the pond. 10 There are boys in the pond.
pages.brief: A wide pond scene. A beaver swims near a pile of sticks and mud at the water's edge, its head above the surface. Close by, two boys stand in the shallow water, splashing and looking at the beaver.

books.title: Gobi Desert Animals
books.art_why: Real animals exist today, so photographs fit.

pages.text: Many animals live in the Gobi Desert. Camels live in the Gobi.
pages.brief: A wide view of the Gobi Desert with several animals visible at a distance, and two camels standing in the foreground. The camels are in the desert where they live. The scene shows the camels among the many animals that live in the Gobi.

pages.text: Eagles live in the Gobi. Grasshoppers live in the Gobi.
pages.brief: An eagle flying above the Gobi Desert, with grasshoppers on the dry ground below. The eagle is in the open sky, and the grasshoppers are among the desert plants. Both are shown in the Gobi Desert where they live.

pages.text: Horses live in the Gobi. Goats live in the Gobi.
pages.brief: Horses standing in the Gobi Desert beside goats. The horses and goats are on dry, open ground in the desert. They are shown in the place where they live, with no other animals added to the scene.

pages.text: Wolves live in the Gobi. Lizards live in the Gobi.
pages.brief: A wolf standing on the dry ground of the Gobi Desert, and a lizard resting on a rock nearby. Both animals are in the desert where they live. The scene shows the wolf and the lizard in the Gobi.

books.title: So Many Shops
books.art_why: Real shops selling bread, fish, flowers, meat, cheese, fruit and vegetables exist today, so photographs fit best.

pages.text: This shop sells bread. This shop sells fish.
pages.brief: Two simple shop scenes side by side. On the left, loaves of bread fill a bakery display. On the right, fresh fish lie on a clean shop display. Both shops are bright and tidy, showing bread and fish for sale.

pages.text: This shop sells flowers. This shop sells meat.
pages.brief: Two simple shop scenes side by side. On the left, bunches of flowers stand in a florist display. On the right, pieces of meat lie in a clean shop display. Both shops are bright and tidy, showing flowers and meat for sale.

pages.text: This shop sells cheese. This shop sells fruit.
pages.brief: Two simple shop scenes side by side. On the left, wheels and blocks of cheese sit on a clean shop display. On the right, fresh fruit is piled in a clean shop display. Both shops are bright and tidy, showing cheese and fruit for sale.

pages.text: This shop sells vegetables. So many shops sell so many things!
pages.brief: A wide row of small shops stands together, with fresh vegetables displayed in front of one shop. Other shop fronts show many goods for sale. The scene is bright and busy, showing that many shops sell many different things.

books.title: Wind Blows
books.art_why: Wind, trees, sand, water, snow and birds are real outdoor subjects for photos.

pages.text: Wind blows on the trees. Wind blows up the sand.
pages.brief: Strong wind bends the branches and leaves of green trees, while loose sand lifts and swirls upward from the ground nearby. The moving air is shown through the swaying trees and the blowing sand, with no people in the outdoor scene.

pages.text: Wind blows over the water. Wind blows across the snow.
pages.brief: Wind moves over a stretch of water, rippling the surface into small waves, and then across snowy ground where loose snow streams sideways. The air feels blustery, with water and snow both shaped by the moving wind. No people are shown.

pages.text: Wind blows away the leaves. Wind blows against the birds.
pages.brief: Loose leaves tumble and scatter away across the ground as wind pushes them, while several birds fly with their bodies angled against the same strong wind. The scene shows only leaves and birds in the moving air.

pages.text: Wind blows through the hair. Wind blows into me!
pages.brief: A child stands outdoors with hair streaming sideways in the wind, eyes squinting slightly as the gust blows into their face and chest. The wind presses clothing and hair, showing it reaching the child directly.

books.title: Animals Can Move
books.art_why: All the animals are real and can be photographed today.

pages.text: The camel can walk.
pages.brief: A camel with a sandy brown coat walks steadily across open desert dunes, long legs mid-stride, head level. Pale sand stretches behind and in front of it under a wide, bright sky, with a few low dunes rolling into the distance.

pages.text: The horse can run.
pages.brief: A horse gallops across a green grassy field, mane and tail lifted by its speed, hooves kicking up small clouds of dust. Fence posts and trees sit far behind it, and the open meadow runs back to a soft line of hills.

pages.text: The snake can slither.
pages.brief: A long snake slithers over dry ground, its body curving in a loose S shape, close to the soil. Small stones, patches of sand and a few tufts of dry grass lie around it, with more bare earth stretching away in the background.

pages.text: The rabbit can hop.
pages.brief: A rabbit hops through low green grass, both back legs pushing off the ground, ears up and front paws tucked. Soft blades of grass surround it, and a few small wildflowers and a blurred hedgerow fill the space behind.

pages.text: The polar bear can swim.
pages.brief: A polar bear swims through dark, icy sea water, head and broad shoulders above the surface, front paws paddling. Chunks of white ice float nearby and a pale, cold sky rests above the flat water behind it.

pages.text: The bird can fly.
pages.brief: A bird flies high in a clear blue sky, wings spread wide, feathers catching the light. Thin clouds drift far below and around it, and the open air stretches out on every side with no ground in sight.

pages.text: The bug can crawl.
pages.brief: A small bug crawls along a broad green leaf, legs gripping the surface, its rounded body close to the plant. The leaf fills most of the view, with soft green stems and other leaves blurred behind it.

pages.text: How can these animals move?
pages.brief: A camel, a horse, a snake, a rabbit, a polar bear, a bird and a bug are shown together, each one in its own patch of desert, field, water, grass or sky, all of them caught mid-movement as if asking how they travel.

books.title: Animal Sounds
books.art_why: The book shows real animals and a real dad, all things that can be photographed today.

pages.text: Dogs bark.
pages.brief: A dog is shown barking, its mouth open as it makes the barking sound. The picture focuses only on the dog and the action of barking, matching the page's simple statement. No other animals or people are added to the scene.

pages.text: Cats meow.
pages.brief: A cat is shown meowing, with the meowing action as the clear focus. The picture keeps only to the cat and its sound, matching the page's simple statement. No other animals or people are added to the scene.

pages.text: Cows moo.
pages.brief: A cow is shown mooing, with the mooing action as the clear focus. The picture keeps only to the cow and its sound, matching the page's simple statement. No other animals or people are added to the scene.

pages.text: Pigs oink.
pages.brief: A pig is shown oinking, with the oinking action as the clear focus. The picture keeps only to the pig and its sound, matching the page's simple statement. No other animals or people are added to the scene.

pages.text: Birds chirp.
pages.brief: Birds are shown chirping, with the chirping action as the clear focus. The picture keeps only to the birds and their sound, matching the page's simple statement. No other animals or people are added to the scene.

pages.text: Ducks quack.
pages.brief: A duck is shown quacking, with the quacking action as the clear focus. The picture keeps only to the duck and its sound, matching the page's simple statement. No other animals or people are added to the scene.

pages.text: Snakes hiss.
pages.brief: A snake is shown hissing, with the hissing action as the clear focus. The picture keeps only to the snake and its sound, matching the page's simple statement. No other animals or people are added to the scene.

pages.text: Bees buzz.
pages.brief: A bee is shown buzzing, with the buzzing action as the clear focus. The picture keeps only to the bee and its sound, matching the page's simple statement. No other animals or people are added to the scene.

pages.text: Lions roar.
pages.brief: A lion is shown roaring, with the roaring action as the clear focus. The picture keeps only to the lion and its sound, matching the page's simple statement. No other animals or people are added to the scene.

pages.text: Dads snore.
pages.brief: A dad is shown sleeping and snoring, with the snoring action as the focus. The picture keeps to this everyday moment and does not add other people or objects beyond the dad and his snoring.

books.title: Bananas Sometimes
books.art_why: Bananas are real everyday fruit, so real photographs suit every page.

pages.text: Bananas sometimes look like hands. Bananas sometimes look like boats.
pages.brief: Two ripe yellow bananas lying on a clean kitchen table, one curved bunch shaped like an open hand with fingers, the other bent upward at both ends like a little boat, both shown clearly in soft daylight.

pages.text: Bananas sometimes look like pencils. Bananas sometimes look like spiders.
pages.brief: Two yellow bananas side by side on a plain wooden surface, one long and straight like a pencil, the other with its peel split into thin curling strips spreading out like spider legs, shown close up in bright light.

pages.text: Bananas sometimes look like telephones. Bananas sometimes look like smiles.
pages.brief: Two yellow bananas on a light tabletop, one curved with a small stem end like a telephone receiver held up, the other bending upward in a wide cheerful curve like a smiling mouth, both clearly visible.

pages.text: Bananas sometimes look like frowns. Bananas always look good to eat.
pages.brief: A small bunch of ripe yellow bananas on a table, one curving downward in a sad frowning shape beside fresh yellow bananas that look ready to eat, shown close up in warm kitchen light.
